The relevant check is **`readability-trailing-comma`**. It controls whether to add, remove, or ignore trailing commas in multi-line enum definitions and initializer lists.

Key details:

- **Options**: Valid values are: Append (add trailing commas where missing), Remove (remove trailing commas where present), and Ignore (do not check multi-line constructs). Default is Append.
- **Behavior**: The check looks for presence or absence of trailing commas in enum definitions and initializer lists, supporting separate policies for single-line and multi-line constructs. By default, it enforces trailing commas in multi-line constructs and removes them from single-line constructs.
- **Rationale for trailing commas**: Trailing commas in multi-line constructs make diffs smaller and easier to read since adding or removing elements only changes a single line, help formatters produce a more desired style, and let code generators avoid special handling of the last element.
- **Limitation**: The check currently doesn't analyze code inside macros.

So if you want clang-tidy to **remove** trailing commas from braced initializer lists (single-line or multi-line), you'd configure `readability-trailing-comma` with the `Remove` option (e.g., for multi-line constructs) — noting that by default single-line constructs already have trailing commas removed, while multi-line ones get them added unless you explicitly set the policy to `Remove`.

More details are available at the [official documentation page](https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/checks/readability/trailing-comma.html).

# Strip trailing commas in initializer lists

## Context

`.clang-format` (added earlier in this branch) forces every element of a
braced initializer list onto its own line whenever the list already ends with
a trailing comma — this is a documented clang-format heuristic, not something
`.clang-format` options can disable. Since some contributors habitually add a
trailing comma after the last element of a struct/array initializer and
others don't, the same logical struct now formats wildly differently
depending on who last touched it (see the compact `.bcs = { {...}, {...}, }`
example vs. the exploded one-line-per-field version clang-format produces
today). The fix is to make "no trailing comma before a closing brace" part of

     though the current codebase is C-heavy, since `.cpp`/`.hpp` files are in
     scope and raw strings are valid C++11 that could show up later.
   Everything not inside one of the above regions (i.e. real code) passes
   through unmasked.
2. On the masked text, find every span matching `,\s*\}` (a comma, only
   whitespace between it and the next `}` — comment/string contents are
   already blanked to spaces so they fall out of `\s*` naturally).
3. For each match, delete just the comma character at that offset from the
   *original* text (leave the whitespace/comments in place). Apply deletions
   from the end of the file backward so earlier offsets stay valid.
4. Write the file back only if it actually changed.

This covers struct/array initializers and enum definitions (both use `, }`),
handles nesting correctly (each comma-before-`}` is found independently), and
can never break compilation — removing a trailing comma before `}` is always
valid C/C++.

Reuse the exact same scope as clang-format: `.c/.h/.cpp/.hpp/.cu/.cuh`,
excluding `*/ker/*` and `core/minus/` — those files must never be touched by
either tool.

new script before clang-format:

  `clang-format -i "$f"`.
- `--check` mode: run `python3 ci/strip-trailing-commas.py --check "$f"` in
  addition to the existing `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` check; fail

'^core/minus/'` pipeline) is reused unchanged.

### 3. Pre-commit hook (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`)

script) *before* the existing clang-format mirror entry, so ordering within
pre-commit's sequential hook execution matches the manual script:


content.text: Found a real bug: masking string literal *contents* to spaces made the regex treat a string-literal array element as if it were empty whitespace, causing a false-positive across `"block-topology" "multi-block-meta"` (a separate pre-existing missing-comma issue in that file, unrelated to my change) — the masked comma+comment+two string literals collapsed into what looked like `,\s*}`. Comments should mask to whitespace (they're trivia), but string/char literal content must mask to a non-whitespace filler so it still "blocks" the regex as real content.

content.text:
It's just clang-format's column-limit wrapping interacting with where each element starts on the line — nothing broken, no interaction with the trailing-comma stripper or `Cpp11BracedListStyle`.

The first `{...}` element sits glued onto the same line as `.poisson_bcs = { `, so it inherits that as a horizontal prefix:

```
    .poisson_bcs = { { .dir = 0, .edge = GKYL_LOWER_EDGE, .type = GKYL_BC_GK_FIELD_DIRICHLET, .value = { 0.0 } },
```
That's `.poisson_bcs = { ` (21 cols) + the struct literal itself (92 cols) = **113 columns** — over the 100-column limit — so clang-format falls back to breaking that element field-by-field onto its own lines.

The second element starts fresh on its own continuation line at the array's actual indent depth (6 spaces), not inheriting that prefix:
```
      { .dir = 0, .edge = GKYL_UPPER_EDGE, .type = GKYL_BC_GK_FIELD_DIRICHLET, .value = { 0.0 } } },
```
That's exactly 100 columns — just barely fits — so it stays compact.

So the asymmetry is purely because element 1 pays for `.poisson_bcs = { ` out of its column budget and element 2 doesn't, combined with this struct being just long enough (extra `.value = { 0.0 }` field, longer `GKYL_BC_GK_FIELD_DIRICHLET` name) to sit right on that boundary. It's the same underlying class of issue as the trailing-comma bug you found earlier — clang-format's per-element wrapping decisions are sensitive to incidental horizontal position, not just logical structure — but there's no equivalent easy mechanical fix here (unlike the trailing comma, there's no "always/never" option that forces the outer brace onto its own line for initializer lists in general).

is there an clang-format option for the opening curly brace to always stay on the same line, and have a line break after it? but perhaps without affecting the placement of the closing curly brace. Would that solve this discrepancy?

No — that specific combination doesn't exist for `{}` initializer lists in clang-format.

The option with exactly that shape — "always break right after the open bracket, don't move the closer" — is `AlignAfterOpenBracket: AlwaysBreak` (or `BlockIndent`, which also block-indents the contents). But per clang-format's own docs, `AlignAfterOpenBracket` only applies to **round brackets, angle brackets, and square brackets** — parentheses in function calls/declarations and template argument lists, and `[]`. It explicitly does not cover curly braces of aggregate initializers. There's no `BraceWrapping`-style sub-option for initializer lists either (that struct only covers control statements, functions, classes/structs/unions, enums, namespaces, extern blocks — not `{}` init expressions). This is a known, longstanding gap in clang-format: braced-init-list line-breaking is governed almost entirely by the column-limit-driven heuristic (plus the trailing-comma-forces-explosion behavior, and `Cpp11BracedListStyle` for spacing only), with no manual "always/never break after `{`" knob.

Even if it did exist and applied to `{}`, it likely wouldn't solve this cleanly: to fix your `poisson_bcs` example, the break would need to be conditional ("break after `{` only when the first element wouldn't otherwise fit") — an unconditional "always break after `{`" would instead blow up your compact cases (`.bcs = { {...}, {...} }`, `.dir = { 0, 2, 2 }`) into multi-line every time, trading one inconsistency for a worse regression elsewhere. The root cause — the first element's column budget depending on how much text already precedes it on that line — isn't something any single clang-format option currently targets.

**New tool:** `ci/strip-trailing-commas.py` — a dependency-free Python script that removes any comma immediately before a closing `}` in initializer lists, since clang-format explodes a braced list onto one line per element whenever a trailing comma is present. It's comment/string/raw-string-literal-aware (won't touch commas inside those) and supports `--check` for CI-style verification.

**Wired in everywhere clang-format already runs**, always *before* clang-format so the comma is gone by the time it formats:
- `ci/format-all.sh` — runs the stripper then clang-format, in both normal and `--check` modes.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — new local hook (`strip-trailing-commas`) ahead of the existing `clang-format` hook.
- CI needs no changes — `.github/workflows/format-check.yml` already runs `pre-commit/action`, which auto-picks up the new hook.
- `README.md` and `.agents/skills/code_style/SKILL.md` — documented the new behavior.

**Style change:** `.clang-format` — added `Cpp11BracedListStyle: false`, so braced initializers get spaces inside (`{ 1, 2, 3 }` instead of `{1, 2, 3}`), independent of the trailing-comma fix.

**One-time repo-wide sweep:** ran both tools across the whole repo — 970 tracked files reformatted (existing trailing commas stripped, then re-run through clang-format with the new brace spacing).
